label: Gallbladder cancer

approval.note: Draft checklist from the NCG GI draft 2021 (gall bladder cancer): needs a clinician's check

site_note: V2 item 5.3 (two primaries): only on a Case File linked to the same patient's other Case File, and only for histopathology, cytology, IHC and molecular records: among several candidates for one record, or several documents carrying a required value, one that names another protocol's site and not this one steps aside and is named on the row for review; a document naming no site never does, and when every candidate names another site every candidate stays. Organ words only. A preference, never a filter; a patient with one cancer is checked as before.
note: Draft checklist from the NCG GI draft guidelines of 15 Jan 2021 on gall bladder cancer (page 1: basic work-up and the four-way split; page 2: per primum; page 3: incidental; page 4: locally advanced; page 5: metastatic) and its radiology synoptic (pages 1 and 2): needs a clinician's check. The files print no tier letters (only 'Optional:' and '(optimal)'), so every tier is a proposal, to be confirmed by the hospital Tumour Board (clinical review before real use). The system records the stage as written (the book names no staging edition) and never computes it; no treatment advice. India first: the National Cancer Grid draft is the only source; it advises radical surgery only where expertise and facilities exist (page 2), and the high share of incidental disease is the Indian presentation it shows (page 3).
settings_note: The setting of the Case File, chosen by the clinician from what the signed reports record (the system never computes a stage and never decides the setting). Each record carries its tier per setting; until a setting is recorded the strictest tier applies. Draft checklist: needs a clinician's check.

post_board.record_fields_source: EUSOMA 2020 (names of all participants, evidence on decisions); Victorian Cancer MDM quality framework 2018 (report errors/changes raised, divergent recommendations and dissenting clinicians); PM-JAY HBP 2.2 s.3.9 (tumour board decision and treatment plan)

policy_basis: PM-JAY Health Benefit Package 2.2 user guidelines (NHA, 2021), section 3.9: pre-authorization is mandatory at each step of cancer care and the decision on appropriate care is to be taken by a multidisciplinary tumour board; NHS England MDT streamlining guidance (2020) pre-listing conditions. The NCG book itself asks for the board: "discussed in MDT)" (NCG GI draft 2021: Gall bladder cancer, page 2); the Tumour Board Case File is that discussion, so no separate record is required for it (orchestrator, night-v3 Phase 2).
